clue.text: Musical creatures endlessly keeping benefit back

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: mice are small creatures

indicators.note: back signals that the benefit word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the dole is unemployment benefit in Britain

explanation.surface: Some animals with musical talent are stingily holding back somebody's benefit payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves MIC; 'back' gives ELOD, which MIC is 'keeping' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic is a straightforward synonym of musical, describing something tuneful.

clue.text: House associated with drink for an officer in China

indicators.note: in tells us the china word holds the article and the officer within it

parts.note: Ming is fine Chinese porcelain, so china
an gives A
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A drinking house for an army officer stationed in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it means porcelain, Ming being a famous Chinese ware.
explanation.definitionFit: A malting is a building where barley is turned into malt for brewing beer and whisky.

clue.text: 13 closed to workers with crazy note about their heart

indicators.note: about means going around another piece

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy

indicators.note: their heart points to the middle letter of the word workers

parts.note: ut is the old name for the first note of the scale, now doh

explanation.surface: Gates are shut on the workforce by a mad memo about what matters to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is GATES. 'their heart' refers to the workers, giving K, the middle letter of 'workers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockout is an employer shutting the factory gates against the workforce in a dispute.

clue.text: See 18
Honorary cleric misrepresented in history

indicators.note: misrepresented signals the letters are shown in a wrong order

parts.note: HON is the abbreviation for honorary

explanation.surface: An honorary churchman has been portrayed wrongly in the historical record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' shuffles HON and CLERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written record of events in order, a history.

clue.text: Cardinal point included by reporter

indicators.note: included by means placed inside another word

parts.note: Cardinal John Henry Newman, the Victorian churchman
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A compass point has been worked into a journalist's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal point' reads as one phrase meaning a compass direction, but 'Cardinal' is Newman the churchman and 'point' alone gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a journalist, someone who reports the news.

clue.text: Hoon's off to start war, as Tweedledum said

indicators.note: off signals that the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: Geoff Hoon was the British Defence Secretary during the Iraq war

indicators.note: to start points to the first letter of the word war

explanation.surface: A defence minister is leaving to begin a war, as a character in Alice said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges HOON to NOHO, then W begins 'war'. Tweedledum, in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, says 'Contrariwise' and 'Nohow!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedledum's catchphrase in the Alice book is the old dialect word for 'not at all'.

clue.text: European at preliminary contest of 22 20 character

indicators.note: at means placed next to the following piece

parts.note: a white person, of European descent
a heat is a qualifying race before a final

explanation.surface: A European takes part in an early race.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 20 is INCANDESCENT; white heat is the glow of something incandescent.
explanation.definitionFit: White heat is the extreme temperature at which metal glows white, the state of being incandescent.

clue.text: I leave cleric in 15

indicators.note: leave means the I departs from the cleric word

parts.note: a minister is a clergyman

explanation.surface: I am quitting the clergyman's post in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is CATHEDRAL, and a minster is a large church of that kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a great church, as in York Minster, often a cathedral.

clue.text: Wild and sure to succeed, as you would expect

definitions.meaning: in an untouched state, not cultivated
a person with a gift for something is certain to do well at it

explanation.definitionFit: Natural means untamed, describes someone with a born talent, and means ordinary or to be expected.

clue.text: Possible sound of one without a coat

indicators.note: possible sound of means the clue words are said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: someone without a thing lacks it, so is a lacker

explanation.surface: Someone without a coat might make a certain noise, perhaps a shiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a glossy varnish applied as a protective coat.

clue.text: Overhead protection from the rain

indicators.note: from here signals that the letters are made out of the following words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat or umbrella gives you cover against wet weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a loose anagram signal: the letters of THE RAIN are rearranged to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is worn over the head to protect the hair, so it is a covering for the top of you.

clue.text: Pass fellow in unusual kit at the moment

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another
unusual signals that the letters of kit are rearranged

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
at the moment means now

explanation.surface: A university fellow wearing strange gear walks by just now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns the kit letters into ITK, with the fellow placed after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'pass' in a quiz is an admission that you have no idea of the answer.

clue.text: Woodworker deprived of fish to go through …

indicators.note: deprived of means the fish is removed from the woodworker

parts.note: a carpenter works with wood
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A carpenter who has lost his fish has to pass through somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go in, to pass through a door or gateway.

clue.text: … Bill for PCs

parts.note: the surname of the founder of Microsoft, whose software runs on personal computers; read on from the previous clue it also means things to go through

explanation.surface: A bill presented for computers, following on from going through something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 12-across: 'to go through … Bill' also points to openings in fences that you walk through.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft, is the best-known name behind PC software.

clue.text: Children's organisation for latter-day Noah?

indicators.note: organisation signals that the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A charity for children names a modern-day ark builder.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of 'Children's' does give an S. Oskar Schindler saved Jews in the war, as Noah saved creatures in the ark; Schindler's Ark was Keneally's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oskar Schindler, like Noah with his ark, rescued many lives from destruction.

clue.text: Church creature finds cure without physician

parts.note: a cat is a creature

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the cure word goes around the physician

parts.note: to cure is to heal
DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a physician

explanation.surface: An animal discovers a remedy without needing a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a large church, the seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Review the situation as rustlers do

definitions.meaning: to pause and assess how things stand
cattle thieves make off with livestock

explanation.definitionFit: To take stock is to assess things; read literally it is what cattle thieves do with the herd.

clue.text: Hooligan's report of choirboy's wear and where

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the hooligan

indicators.note: report of means the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a ruff is the frilled collar worn by choirboys
the neck is where a ruff is worn

explanation.surface: A hooligan reports on what a choirboy wears and where.
explanation.walkthrough: Choirboys wear a ruff, a frilled collar; 'where' it is worn completes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughneck is a rowdy, uncouth person, much like a hooligan.

clue.text: Being abusive is something to hold onto

definitions.meaning: a fence or bar used for support

explanation.definitionFit: Railing means scolding angrily, and also a barrier of rails to grip.

clue.text: Dirty cow with relatives

parts.note: unclean means dirty
to cow is to intimidate, to daunt

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a woman and her family.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters split as UNCLE AND AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle and an aunt are family members, relatives.

clue.text: Ebbing and flowing from Mount Ida lately

indicators.note: from here signals that the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Water ebbs and flows down from Mount Ida recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes water that rises and falls with the tides.

clue.text: See 22
15 president left depression in pub

indicators.note: in tells us the depression sits within the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a col is a dip between mountain peaks

explanation.surface: The president left a hollow in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is CATHEDRAL: Lincoln has a famous cathedral and gave its name to a US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is a cathedral city and Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth US president.

clue.text: Furious with Peruvian ancestry?

definitions.meaning: white-hot with rage, glowing with anger
being descended from the people of the old empire of Peru

explanation.walkthrough: Split the twelve letters as INCAN DESCENT for the second reading; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incandescent is blazing with fury; read in two words, it means coming from the Inca people of Peru.

clue.text: Fitting destination and surroundings of Great Ouse or Nene

parts.note: the Wash is the bay on England's east coast where the Great Ouse and Nene end

parts.words: surroundings of Great Ouse or Nene
parts.note: a river's basin is the land it drains, its surroundings

explanation.surface: A geography lesson on where two East Anglian rivers end up and the land around them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Ouse and Nene are English rivers that flow into the Wash; 'destination' borrows the 'of Great Ouse or Nene' that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is a bathroom fitting, a sink for washing hands.

clue.text: Archetypal invention with list

parts.note: a ship that lists heels over

explanation.surface: The classic invention comes with a register.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheel is the stock example of a great invention, as in 'reinventing the wheel'.

clue.text: Judge hasn't a right to be the mordant type

indicators.note: hasn't means these letters are missing from the judge word

parts.note: an arbiter is a judge

explanation.surface: A judge lacking a sense of rightness turns out to be cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mordant' means biting, so it describes one who bites.
explanation.definitionFit: A biter is one who bites, and mordant comes from the Latin for biting.

clue.text: Traveller of low degree needs company, I feel

indicators.note: needs is a loose signal here, as if the letters were kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: A humble wanderer longs for companionship, in my opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is the anagram signal, perhaps a pun on 'kneads': rearrange CO and I FEEL. 'of low degree' means at a low temperature, not humble.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice floe drifts on the sea, a traveller at a very cold temperature.

clue.text: Active personality follows head from part of year

indicators.note: follows means this piece comes after the other
head from means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a month is part of a year
the ego is the self, the personality

explanation.surface: A lively character comes after the head of the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head from' leaves ONTH; the personality 'follows' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is busy and active, always moving.

clue.text: Far from private

parts.note: the opposite of a private: both public in scope and the top army rank, far above a private soldier

explanation.definitionFit: General means widespread rather than personal, and is also the highest army rank, far above a private.

clue.text: Constituent of beak whose end takes time to preserve

definitions.text: Constituent of beak whose end takes time to preserve

indicators.note: whose end points to the final letter of the word beak

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to tin food is to preserve it in a can

explanation.surface: Part of a bird's bill whose tip takes a long time to keep.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the end of 'beak' plus ERA and TIN builds the substance a beak is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratin is the fibrous protein that makes up beaks, horns, hair and nails.
